newsArray.title: Burras get first win of season
newsArray.description: It was a consistent and determined effort that earned Minyip Murtoa their first win of the season on Saturday, according to coach Luke Fisher. "We started very well and, besides a period in the third when we let them kick a couple of goals in a row, we were consistent for the day," Fisher said. "The boys were very happy and relieved to finally get the reward in the score and by singing the song. "They really deserved it." The coach added they nearly lifted the roof off the changerooms in belting out their club song after the win and they had plenty of supporters sharing in their success. With the last match between Dimboola and Minyip Murtoa having ended in a draw, the Burras were going to do everything they could to get the win this time. They kicked off the game brilliantly and held a 47-point lead at the end of the first quarter before holding an advantage of 54 points at half-time. Dimboola, to their credit, were better in the final half, but the Burras weren't going to let this one slip, scoring 5.1 to the opposition's 3.2 in quarter three and 2.6 to the Roos' 3.4 in the final quarter. The Burras coach was named best on ground, along with forward Oscar Gawith, with an eight-goal haul. Mitchell O'Donnell and Simon Hobbs were the better players in the losing side, while the majority of their goals came from Brayden Culhane, Darcy Dubois and Thomas ODwyer, who each booted two. Fisher said Gawith in his efforts was "unreal". "He had 20 shots on goal and really could have gone away with a bigger bag of goals," Fisher said. But what pleased the coach most was the fact the Burras played the game as a team and remained disciplined to it all match. "We set out to limit the impact of some of their better players and we were able to do that," Fisher said in his post-game reflection. "We played a much more team-oriented game and we were much better at our forward entry kick than last time we played them. "Lots of players played really well. "Our theme for the day was for everyone to get a lick of the ice-cream, and everyone certainly did that. "But Ryder Hudson, a 15-year-old playing a key position, was also good in the backline."
